partners.mechanism_chain: SOX9 (HGNC:11145) —DISRUPTS→ chondrogenesis; GATA4 (HGNC:4156) —DISRUPTS→ cardiac septation; chondrogenesis —LEADS_TO→ Campomelic dysplasia (MONDO:0007251); cardiac septation —LEADS_TO→ Ventricular septal defect (MONDO:0013746); SOX9 (HGNC:11145) —DISRUPTS→ cardiac septation; GATA4 (HGNC:4156) —DISRUPTS→ chondrogenesis. Both SOX9 and GATA4 are crucial transcription factors involved in embryonic development. SOX9 is essential for chondrogenesis and also plays a role in cardiac development, while GATA4 is a master regulator of cardiac development and also influences skeletal development. Haploinsufficiency in SOX9 leads to campomelic dysplasia by disrupting chondrogenesis and also contributes to cardiac defects. Haploinsufficiency in GATA4 leads to ventricular septal defects by disrupting cardiac septation, and it can also affect skeletal development. The convergence occurs on the pathways of chondrogenesis and cardiac septation, which are both modulated by these shared genes.
